annotation_description: Choosing to go first in a 4-player multiplayer game is generally suboptimal. Going first means you draw fewer cards over the course of the early game compared to going later in turn order. In multiplayer, the advantage of playing first is diminished because you have three opponents rather than one, and the extra card from drawing is more valuable. Additionally, the hand has only one land (Forest) and will likely need to mulligan anyway, so going first with a weak hand provides no tempo advantage.

message: Select a card (2 more) to put on the bottom of your library
annotation_description: Bottoming Warstorm Surge means the final 5-card hand will be Sol Ring + 4 lands with zero spells, entirely reliant on topdecking. Warstorm Surge is one of the best cards in a Vrondiss deck - each dragon token triggers 5 damage to any target. With Sol Ring, it could be cast as early as turn 3-4.

message: Select a card (1 more) to put on the bottom of your library
annotation_description: Mosswort Bridge is a reasonable card to bottom in a vacuum, but in a Vrondiss deck that naturally creates 5/4 tokens, reaching 10 total power for Mosswort Bridge's activation is trivially easy. Mosswort Bridge lets you play a card for free, which is extremely powerful. One of the basic Forests or Mountains would have been a better bottom choice since the deck likely has plenty of basic lands, while Mosswort Bridge provides unique free-cast utility that synergizes perfectly with the commander's token generation.

Playing Prosperous Innkeeper before playing the Barren Moor land is a sequencing error. With only 2 lands on the battlefield (Jungle Hollow and Tainted Wood), playing Barren Moor first would give 3 lands, then next turn they could have 4 mana available. By casting the Innkeeper first (using both lands), they miss the opportunity to play Barren Moor this turn since it should be played before spending mana. The Innkeeper creates a Treasure token which partially compensates, but playing the land first is strictly better sequencing - it doesn't change the ability to cast Innkeeper this turn (2 mana available either way) and ensures the land drop isn't missed.
Declined to attack with Prosperous Innkeeper when no opponents had blockers available. While 1 damage is minimal in Commander, it was completely free with zero risk.

Passed the turn with exactly 4 mana available and Seer's Sundial in hand, the only castable spell. No instant-speed plays in hand to justify holding up mana. Every turn Seer's Sundial is delayed is a potential card draw missed from future land drops.

The player's reasoning says they want to cast Colossal Majesty (which costs {2}{G} and they have the mana for it with 2 Forests + Sol Ring), but they actually played Haven of the Spirit Dragon instead. Colossal Majesty is a key card draw engine, and while they have no creatures with power 4+ yet, casting it now sets up future card advantage once they deploy their commander Vrondiss (5/4). Playing Haven of the Spirit Dragon as the land drop is fine, but the player should have ALSO cast Colossal Majesty with their available mana (2 Forests + Sol Ring = 2G + 2C, more than enough for {2}{G}). Instead, it appears they only played the land and didn't cast Colossal Majesty despite having the mana and intending to do so based on their reasoning.

GLM47 Sarge has 4 lands in play (Jungle Hollow, Tainted Wood, Temple of Malady, and the Prosperous Innkeeper's Treasure token from entering). They have Exotic Orchard in hand and chose not to play it. With Exotic Orchard + existing lands, they could have 5 mana sources next turn. More importantly, they have Chatterfang (3 mana) available to cast this turn - they have 3 untapped lands (Tainted Wood, Temple of Malady, and one other) plus could play Exotic Orchard first. Wait - looking more carefully, the lands may be tapped from earlier plays. But the decision shows Chatterfang as a valid choice, meaning they have the mana to cast it. Playing Exotic Orchard first (it enters untapped since it's not a tapland) and then casting Chatterfang would be optimal - getting the 3/3 commander on board early with forestwalk and the token-doubling ability. Even if they can't cast Chatterfang this turn, they should at minimum play the Exotic Orchard to not miss a land drop.

Failed to cast Colossal Majesty ({2}{G}) with available mana (Forest + Sol Ring). While they have no creatures with power 4+ yet, deploying this card advantage enchantment early ensures it's ready to trigger as soon as a large creature (like Vrondiss 5/4) hits the board. The mana was otherwise going to waste.

With only 5 lands and no Sol Ring, casting Maskwood Nexus (4 mana) uses the entire turn but provides minimal immediate value - just making creatures all types. Chatterfang (3 mana) would leave mana open, provide a 3/3 body with forestwalk, and start generating squirrel tokens for future plays. Chatterfang also synergizes much better with the hand (The Odd Acorn Gang, Shamanic Revelation, End-Raze Forerunners) by building a board presence. Maskwood Nexus's creature type ability is largely irrelevant without a tribal payoff beyond Chatterfang's squirrel sacrifice ability, and its token-making ability costs 3 more mana. Chatterfang would have been the stronger play to start building board presence toward the powerful cards in hand.

The player has an Island and a Plains in hand and has an untapped Plains and an untapped land available. They should play one of their land cards to avoid missing a land drop. They have mana available and Brainstorm in hand which could also be cast. Playing a land is free value and missing land drops in the early-to-mid game is a real cost, especially when holding cards like Mammoth Umbra (5 mana) that need more lands to cast.

Casting Anya before combat is suboptimal when the player has Lightning Greaves in hand and plans to equip it for haste anyway. However, the bigger sequencing issue is that the player should play their Mountain land drop first before casting spells, to have access to more mana and to potentially trigger Seer's Sundial (paying 2 to draw a card). With 5 lands + Seer's Sundial on board, playing Mountain first gives 6 lands and the option to pay 2 for a card draw. After playing Mountain (6 lands), they'd have enough mana to: play land (free) → potentially pay 2 for Sundial draw → cast Anya (5 mana) → cast Lightning Greaves (2 mana) → equip (0 mana), though that would require 9 mana total (2+5+2=9) and they'd only have 7 mana from 6 lands. Actually with 6 lands they have 6 mana, so they can cast Anya (5) and Lightning Greaves (2) = 7, which doesn't work. With 5 lands currently they have 5 mana available. Playing Mountain first gives 6 mana. They need 5 for Anya + 2 for Greaves = 7. Either way they can't cast both in one turn without more mana. But playing the land first before casting spells is still correct sequencing to maximize options and potentially trigger Seer's Sundial.

Played a land before casting Brainstorm. With two excess Plains in hand, casting Brainstorm first would allow drawing 3 cards, putting back redundant Plains on top, and then making a more informed land drop. This is a classic Brainstorm sequencing mistake.

Cycling Decree of Savagery for 6 mana with no creatures on board wastes the +1/+1 counter ability entirely, paying 6 mana just to draw one card. Meanwhile, Return to Nature for 2 mana could destroy Maskwood Nexus (a key enabler for Chatterfang) or other problematic permanents, leaving 5 mana to deploy Dragon's Hoard and Dragonmaster Outcast in the same turn.

annotation_description: Mask of Avacyn is not equipped to anything - it's just sitting on the battlefield doing nothing currently. Meanwhile, Maskwood Nexus is actively making all of GLM47 Sarge's creatures every creature type (enabling Chatterfang synergies and making the token-creation ability produce extra squirrels), and Seer's Sundial provides Kimi25 Analyst ongoing card advantage. Azorius Signet is also a more impactful target as it's Haiku Vorthos's mana acceleration. Destroying an unequipped equipment that costs 3 to equip is very low value compared to these alternatives.

Casting Desolation Giant without kicker ({W}{W}) only destroys all OTHER creatures Kimi25 Analyst controls. Kimi25 Analyst has no other creatures on the battlefield - Lightning Greaves and Seer's Sundial are artifacts, not creatures. So the ETB trigger destroys nothing, making it just a vanilla 3/3 for 4 mana. Meanwhile, Kimi25 Analyst has board wipe potential with the kicked version (costs {2}{R}{R}{W}{W} = 6 mana) which would destroy all other creatures including GLM47 Sarge's Plaguecrafter and Prosperous Innkeeper. With only 4 untapped lands available, the kick isn't possible this turn, but deploying it without kicker wastes the powerful board wipe effect permanently. Faith's Fetters on Maskwood Nexus or Plaguecrafter would have been more impactful, neutralizing a key permanent while gaining 4 life.

Haiku Vorthos passed without playing a land from hand despite having Island and Plains available. Missing a land drop is free value lost, and an extra Plains would power up Armored Ascension later. With 4 cards in hand and no creatures yet, hitting land drops is critical to eventually deploying threats with equipment/auras.

Squirrel Nest provides slow incremental value (one 1/1 per turn) while The Odd Acorn Gang would be an immediate 5/5 with menace, trample, and reach that synergizes powerfully with Maskwood Nexus (all creatures are Squirrels, so they can all use the pump ability). The Odd Acorn Gang also draws cards when Squirrels deal combat damage, providing much faster board impact.

Enchanting Temple of Malady with Squirrel Nest removes a dual-colored mana source (B/G) from mana production. Since Squirrel Nest replaces the land's abilities with just token production, GLM47 Sarge loses access to a colored mana source. Exotic Orchard would be a better target since it only produces mana based on opponents' lands and is less critical, or even better, putting it on a basic Swamp would preserve the dual-land's flexibility. With cards like End-Raze Forerunners (5GGG) and The Odd Acorn Gang (3BG) in hand requiring significant colored mana, losing a BG dual land hurts casting ability.

Casting Hunted Dragon gives an opponent three 2/2 Knight tokens with first strike. In a multiplayer game where Kimi25 has no board presence besides equipment and lands, giving free creatures to an opponent is a significant downside. Additionally, playing Ancient Amphitheater first (revealing Hunted Dragon as a Giant) would let it enter untapped, providing an extra land. More importantly, Warstorm Surge at 6 mana could be cast next turn and would provide much more lasting value, turning every future creature into removal. Faith's Fetters on the Neverwinter Hydra (which is likely a significant threat from Gem25F at 19hp) would neutralize a threat and gain 4 life.

Hunted Dragon's ETB gives an opponent three 2/2 white Knight tokens with first strike. Giving these to GLM47 Sarge (44 life, highest life total) is one of the worse choices. Gem25F Stoic is at 19 life and is the biggest threat on the board with Neverwinter Hydra — giving them three 2/2s is bad. But Haiku Vorthos has a relatively empty board with no creatures and would benefit least from three 2/2 first strikers since they lack synergies. More importantly, GLM47 Sarge has Prosperous Innkeeper which triggers 'whenever another creature you control enters, you gain 1 life' — and with Maskwood Nexus making all creatures all types, the three Knight tokens entering will each trigger Prosperous Innkeeper, gaining Sarge 3 life. Giving tokens to the player who gains life from creature ETBs is clearly suboptimal.

Gem25F Stoic cast Rishkar's Expertise without first playing Path of Ancestry from hand. Path of Ancestry enters tapped so it doesn't affect mana this turn, but playing it first ensures the land drop isn't wasted. After drawing 9 cards, they won't be able to make a land drop since it's already been used (or in this case, missed entirely).

Rishkar's Expertise was available (shown as 'Unknown' in choices, and visible in hand) but was incorrectly dismissed as 'no longer available.' With Neverwinter Hydra on board (likely with significant +1/+1 counters from d6 rolls), Rishkar's Expertise would draw multiple cards AND allow casting a free spell with MV 5 or less (like Dragon's Hoard or Bag of Tricks). This is substantially more impactful than just casting a single 5/5 flyer.

Playing Island instead of Plains when holding Armored Ascension, which gives +1/+1 for each Plains controlled. With no creatures on board currently, maximizing Plains count for when Armored Ascension can eventually be cast would provide more value.

With all lands and mana sources tapped, GLM47 Sarge likely cannot cast Bastion of Remembrance (costs {2}{B}). The only productive action available should be playing Temple of Malady as a land drop (if they haven't made one this turn). Even if the game engine somehow allows the cast, they should prioritize the land drop first to have mana available.

message: Select a player, planeswalker, or battle to attack
annotation_description: Attacking Gem25F Stoic who has Neverwinter Hydra on board means the Hydra can block one of the attackers (Plaguecrafter 3/2 or Prosperous Innkeeper 1/1), likely killing it and reducing total damage dealt. Haiku Vorthos and Kimi25 Analyst both have no creatures and cannot block, guaranteeing all 4 damage lands.

Player believes Hunted Dragon is already on the battlefield ready to attack, but it's actually still in hand (the Unknown card in choices). They passed without casting anything, missing the opportunity to cast Fellwar Stone (2 mana) then Hunted Dragon (using remaining 3 mana + Fellwar Stone for 5 total). Even though 6 damage doesn't kill Gem25F at 9 life, deploying the threat with haste via Lightning Greaves applies significant pressure. Additionally, at minimum Fellwar Stone should have been cast for mana development.

Gem25F Stoic is at 3 life. Kimi25 Analyst has Meteor Blast in hand, which costs X{R}{R}{R}. With the available untapped lands (2 Plains, 1 Mountain, 1 Mountain) plus Lightning Greaves and Seer's Sundial (non-mana), let me recount: Looking at the battlefield, the tapped lands are 2 Mountains and 1 Plains. Untapped lands are: 2 Plains, 2 Mountains. Plus Fellwar Stone could be cast, but that doesn't help this turn. Meteor Blast for X=1 costs {1}{R}{R}{R} = 4 mana, dealing 4 damage to 1 target. With 2 untapped Plains and 2 untapped Mountains, that's exactly 4 mana (1 generic from Plains + RRR from remaining Plains+2Mountains... wait, Plains don't produce R). Let me recount: Untapped permanents: 2 Plains (W each), 2 Mountains (R each), Seer's Sundial, Lightning Greaves. For Meteor Blast X=1: need RRRR total? No - it's X{R}{R}{R}, so X=1 costs 1+RRR = 4 mana. The 1 generic can come from a Plains, and RRR needs 3 red sources. Only 2 Mountains are untapped, so only 2R available. Can't cast Meteor Blast for X=1. But wait - Fellwar Stone costs {2} and could be cast with the 2 Plains, but it enters tapped... no, Fellwar Stone doesn't enter tapped. Cast Fellwar Stone with 2 Plains, then tap 2 Mountains + Fellwar Stone for RRR+1 colored mana = enough for Meteor Blast X=1 dealing 4 damage to Gem25F Stoic at 3 life, killing them. This is missing lethal on a player at 3 life.

Haiku Vorthos passed their postcombat main phase without playing a land despite having Plains, Island, and Seachrome Coast in hand. Missing a land drop is pure downside, especially when Armored Ascension in hand scales with Plains count.

Gem25F Stoic is at 1 life with no untapped blockers (Neverwinter Hydra is tapped). GLM47 Sarge has multiple creatures available to attack (Prosperous Innkeeper, tokens) and could trivially eliminate an opponent. Leaving an opponent alive at 1 life with card advantage engines (Colossal Majesty, Sol Ring) is extremely dangerous.

message: Select a player, planeswalker, or battle to attack
annotation_description: Attacking the player at 51 life instead of the player at 30 life. With limited attack power, dealing damage to the higher-life player is less impactful. Attacking Kimi25 Analyst at 30 life would bring them closer to dangerous thresholds and is more strategically meaningful.

Haiku Vorthos appears to have no creatures on the battlefield to enchant with Armored Ascension. The reasoning references 'Daxos' but no creature is present on their board. Casting an Aura with no valid target wastes the card and 4 mana.

Seachrome Coast enters tapped since they control more than 2 other lands, providing no mana this turn. Plains would enter untapped and also increase the bonus from Armored Ascension in hand (+1/+1 per Plains). They already have blue mana from Island and Azorius Signet, making the blue from Seachrome Coast redundant.

Failed to play a land before casting Warstorm Surge. They had Mountain, Blasted Landscape, and Command Tower in hand. Playing Command Tower first would give them an extra land on the battlefield for future turns at no cost. Additionally, at 13 life with no creatures to trigger Warstorm Surge immediately, Faith's Fetters (costing only 4 mana, gaining 4 life, and neutralizing a threat) might have been more defensively appropriate.

Haiku Vorthos chose to cast Armored Ascension before playing their Plains from hand. Since Armored Ascension gives +1/+1 per Plains controlled, playing the Plains first would have given an additional +1/+1 (5 Plains instead of 4). The land drop costs nothing and directly buffs the spell.

Kimi25 Analyst is at 6 life with no creatures to block and all lands tapped. GLM47 Sarge has The Odd Acorn Gang (5/5 menace/trample) plus multiple tokens on board. With Maskwood Nexus making everything Squirrels, they could use Squirrel tap abilities to pump The Odd Acorn Gang to 7/7+ and attack for lethal. Additionally, passing without playing Forest (land drop), Sol Ring, or Arcane Signet wastes significant mana development.
